newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peregrine ties GZI Transport's high PE to earnings.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine ties GZI Transport's high PE to earnings.

text.p: Strong earnings prospects justify the high price to earnings (PE) multiple of Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd toll road spinoff GZI Transport Ltd, lead underwriter Peregrine Capital Ltd said on Monday.
"We cannot just look at the PE, we have to take into account its earnings potential," Peregrine Capital chairman Francis Leung told reporters.
"As earnings grow and the price remains steady, the PE will come down later," he said.

GZI Transport said in its listing prospectus that prospective PE for the year ending in December 1997 is 22.12 times on a weighted average basis, with adjusted net tangible asset value at HK$3.54 per share.
There has been some concern in the market that GZI Transport's high PE signals a high listing price, which could affect the subscription response.
GZI's counterparts, toll road operators Road King Infrastructural Ltd and Anhui Expressway Co Ltd, are trading at a prospective PE of 16.84 and 19.17 times, respectively.
GZI Transport said it will issue 250 million shares at HK$3.23, at the high end of a revised prospective range of HK$3.00 to HK$3.25.

It said 187.5 million shares will be placed internationally, with the remaining 62.5 million shares offered in Hong Kong in an initial public offering. Warrants will be attached in the proportion of one warrent for every five shares subscribed.
The IPO will run from January 21-24, with dealing in the shares expected to begin on January 30.
GZI Transport said it has granted Peregrine Capital an over-allotment option to request the company to issue up to 37.5 million additional shares.

Proceeds of the share issue would be used to finance investment in existing and future toll road projects in China. GZI Transport now has six toll road projects, mainly in southern Guangdong province.
"Guangdong is one of the provinces with a large number of cars among other provinces in China," Leung said. "Traffic flow is expected to be booming in the future."
